production.note: US model years. Hagerty: 'Introduced for the 2010 model year'; 'Production of the 458 concluded in 2015, succeeded by the turbocharged 488 GTB'. KBB (kbb-458) lists model years 2010 to 2015 for the 458 Italia. Unveiled in 2009 (Evo: 'At its launch in 2009'; evo-458 titles the car '2009 - 2015'). The 458 Spider and 458 Speciale are separate models.

body.note: Two-seat mid-engined berlinetta; the open car is the separately named 458 Spider.

configuration.note: Ferrari specification list as printed by carsales: 'Type V8 – 90°'

displacementL.note: 4,499 cc. Ferrari specification list as printed by carsales: 'Displacement 4499 cc (274.5 cu in.)'; CAR Magazine's specs panel also gives '4499cc 32v V8' (car-458).

fuel.note: Petrol engine with direct injection ('the company's first mid-mounted direct injection engine'); fuel type inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: CAR Magazine specs panel: 'Seven-speed Getrag twin-clutch auto, rear-wheel drive'

transmission.note: Ferrari specification list as printed by carsales: 'Gearbox: Dual-clutch, 7-speed F1'. Evo: 'seven-speed dual-clutch transmission' (Getrag). No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 570 cv x 0.98632 = 562 hp. Quote (ferrari.com): "It is an entirely new design engineered to reach a maximum of 9,000 rpm – a first on a road car with this cylinder capacity – with a high 12.5:1 compression ratio and a maximum power output of 570 cv." Ferrari's specification list as printed by carsales (carsales-458): "Maximum power 570 CV (425 kW)** @ 9000 rpm", footnote "Including 5 CV of ram effect". No separate SAE rating for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS; US publications print the same 562 hp (Hagerty: '562 horsepower in the Italia and Spider'; Star Tribune US review, March 2010: '562 at 9,000 rpm').

weightLb.note: 1,485 kg x 2.20462 = 3,274 lb (Evo and CAR print it as plain "Weight"; the Star Tribune calls it curb weight). Coupe with the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only transmission). Quote (Evo specification panel for the Ferrari 458 Italia): "Weight | 1485kg". Same figure in CAR Magazine's specs panel (car-458): "Weight / material: 1485kg/aluminium", and in the Star Tribune's US review of March 2010 (startribune-458): curb weight "3,274 pounds". Ferrari's own press specification gives only a dry weight: "Dry weight 1380 kg (3042 lbs)*", footnote "With forged wheels and Racing seats" (carsales-458). The published kerb figure is exactly 105 kg above that optioned dry weight, so it very probably also assumes the optional forged wheels and racing seats. No US-specific figure was found. Under the guide's weight order this is step 3 (a curb weight for a car with lightweight options; here very probably the forged wheels and racing seats named in that footnote), adopted on 2 October 2026: no curb weight for a standard car was found, and a standard car is somewhat heavier.

sources.title: Ferrari 458 (2009 - 2015) review – the last and best supercar of its kind

values.value: 1,380 kg (3,042 lb) dry, with forged wheels and Racing seats

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs curb. Ferrari's press specification lists only a dry weight (no fluids), footnoted 'With forged wheels and Racing seats'; the magazines print the kerb weight.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the published kerb figure under weight step 3 (an optioned car's curb weight), since no standard-car curb weight was found and a curb weight ranks above a dry weight.
